en: The Noble Sūtra of the Heart-mantra of the Glorious Amoghapāśa. Oṃ! Homage to the glorious Lokanātha! Homage to the Blessed One, Amoghapāśa!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount Potalaka,
in the abode of the noble Avalokiteśvara, which was adorned with many *śāla*, *tāla*, *tamāla*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, and *atimuktaka* trees, as well as various jewel-trees,
together with a great saṅgha of monks— eighteen thousand monks and nine hundred and ninety billion nayutas of koṭis of bodhisattvas.
Surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sons of gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm,
the Lord [the Buddha] was teaching the Dharma with reference to the sons of gods of the Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Brahmakāyika realms.
Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat and draped his upper robe over one shoulder.
Placing his right knee upon the ground and joining his palms toward where the Blessed One was,
he bowed down and, with a smiling face, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One,
I possess a heart-mantra named Amoghapāśarāja, which was [attained] by me previously in the ninety-first aeon, Vilokitā."
It was received from the presence of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Lokendrarāja in this world-system,

by which the Blessed One inspired many hundreds of thousands of devaputras— headed by the devaputras Īśvara and Maheśvara, and headed by the devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa realm— to [strive for] unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

And I have attained one million samādhis, headed by the array of non-deluded knowledge (*asaṃmohajñānavyūha*). Furthermore, Blessed One, in whatever region of earth this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* shall circulate,

it should be known, Blessed One, that in that region twelve hundred thousand sons of gods, headed by Īśvara, Maheśvara, and the Brahmakāyikas, will remain for the sake of protection, shelter, and guardianship.
“Blessed One, that spot of earth where this Amoghapāśahṛdaya shall circulate will become worthy of being honored as a caitya.
Blessed One, those beings who hear this Amoghapāśahṛdaya will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas.”

Blessed One, if anyone who is a wrongdoer, a locus of all evils, one who practices sinful dharmas, a reviler of the noble ones, a rejecter of the true Dharma, one destined for the Avīci hell, and a rejecter of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, should feel remorse and undertake restraint for the future;
Blessed One, by the mere practice of fasting and recitation, even in this very life, that karma is purified, brought to total exhaustion, and turned back—
whether it be a fever lasting one day, two days, three days, or four days, or likewise a fever lasting seven days;
or whether it be pain in the eyes, pain in the teeth, pain in the ears, pain in the nose, or pain in the gums, lips, or tongue.
Or by pain in the palate, or pain in the heart, or pain in the abdomen, or pain in the sides, or pain in the hips, or pain in the limbs, or pain in the minor members,
or pain from hemorrhoids or dysentery, or by diarrhea, or by pain in the hands and feet,
or by headache, or by afflictions such as *balāhaka*, *citra-kuṣṭha*, *vicarcikā*, *kiṭibha*, fistula-in-ano, *lohaliṅga*, throat-obstruction, eruptive boils, epilepsy, or spells known as *kākhorda*.
Or by means of killing, binding, beating, threatening, or the invocation of spirits performed against those who have done harm;
in short, Blessed One, that karma goes to complete exhaustion and purification through physical affliction, mental affliction, or the seeing of bad dreams.

How much more so, Blessed One, for those of pure nature who are resolved through faith— be they among the four assemblies or the four castes— even if they are like illusions— if they hear this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of mine, and take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, write it,
cause it to be written, master it, and cause other beings to hear it.
Or, standing at the ear of beings who have fallen into the animal realm, he will whisper these words into their ears and contemplate these mantra-words:

through non-rejection, formlessness, non-conceptualization, non-origination, non-delay, non-action, freedom from afflictions, the settling of the mind in equanimity, and being devoid of the five aggregates.
By this yoga, the recollection of the Buddha (buddhānusmṛti) should be cultivated;
then, thousands of Buddhas from the ten directions will appear before them face-to-face,
and they will perform confession of their transgressions.
And so on;
up to the point that he will have it written in a book and keep it in his home.
What need is there to say more, Blessed One? He will listen even out of mutual rivalry.
Whether out of fear of their master, or by following others, or for the sake of mockery, they shall hear [the sound].
O Blessed One, it should be known that through the power of the noble Avalokiteśvara, that sound will descend and settle within the hollows of their ears.
It is just as if, O Blessed One, some man were to take sandalwood, or camphor, or saffron, or musk, and having dragged it about or reviled it, were to grind it upon a stone or on the ground.
One should smear oneself [with these];
yet that sandalwood, camphor, saffron, and musk do not think, "I have been drawn upon or insulted by this person; therefore, I shall overstep my fragrance.
Rather, it remains simply fragrant.
In the same way, Blessed One, this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* of mine— whether someone should treat it with contempt or derision,
and so forth,
even if they worship it with deceitful words or without any provisions for the journey.
Blessed One, for those harsh beings, that very [act] will become a cause of virtue;
wherever they are reborn, there they shall never be separated from the fragrance of the equipment of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, and merit.
It makes them truly fragrant with ethical discipline.
"O Blessed One, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, monk or nun, layman or laywoman, or any other sentient being, having dedicated themselves to the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya*,
should observe a fast on the eighth day of the bright fortnight;
and should recite the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* seven times without speaking to anyone— O Blessed One, twenty benefits are to be expected for such a person in this very life."
What are the twenty?
Namely: no diseases shall arise in his body;
and whatever diseases have arisen in him shall quickly be pacified through the power of karma.
He will have limbs that are supple, charming, and smooth;
he will be beloved by many people;
and he will obtain secret meanings.
And once it has arisen, thieves cannot take away its wealth;
it is not consumed by fire,
nor is it carried off by water.
The king will not be able to seize it even with his mind;
his undertakings will flourish,
and there will be no fear of lightning or water.
There will be no fear of wind or rain.
Having consecrated ashes or water seven times with the Amoghapāśahṛdaya, one should establish a boundary for the field in all directions, intermediate directions, below, and above;
all calamities will be pacified.
Furthermore, those who steal vitality will not be able to take away his vitality;
he will be dear to all sentient beings and pleasing to them,
and he will have no fear of enemies.
Any fear of enemies that has arisen for him will quickly be pacified;
he shall have no fear of humans,
no fear of *kākhorda* spells, no fear of *ḍākinīs*, and no intense primary or secondary afflictions (*kleśa-upakleśa*) shall arise.
They shall not meet their end by fire, nor by poison, nor by weapons;
wherever they are reborn, there they shall never be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
These twenty benefits are to be expected.
They shall obtain eight further qualities.
Which eight?
At the time of death, the noble Avalokiteśvara will appear face-to-face in the form of a monk.
He will pass away in happiness;
he will not have a confused view.
He will not make a movement of his hands, nor a movement of his feet; he will not discharge excrement or urine, and he will not pass away while mounted [on a vehicle].
His mindfulness will be well-established.
He shall not die with his face turned downward;
at the time of death, he will possess inexhaustible eloquence;
and in whichever Buddha-field he makes a vow, there he will take rebirth.
And he shall not be separated from virtuous friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
It should be recited three times each day, at the three periods of the day.
Indeed, those who desire specific benefits must avoid liquor, meat, onions, leeks, garlic, and food remnants from a refuse heap.
This Dharma discourse called the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* should be heard after one has ascertained the strength and weakness of all sentient beings;
one must not practice the "teacher’s fist.
For it is by having abandoned impurity, stinginess, and envy that beings become Bodhisattvas.

Enlightenment is attained by accomplishing the welfare of sentient beings, and thereby one enters the ranks of the bodhisattvas. Enlightenment is said to consist of wisdom (*prajñā*) and the being (*sattva*), which is skillful means (*upāya*).
These two factors are attained precisely through the accomplishment of the welfare of sentient beings.

“If, Blessed One, you would grant me permission, I shall now proclaim this heart-mantra before the Tathāgata for the sake, welfare, and happiness of the fourfold assembly, and for others who have committed evil deeds.
Then the Blessed One said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara:
“Speak, O Pure Being, whenever you deem it the right time.”
"This has been approved by the Tathāgata; in the future time, in the final age, it will perform the duty of a father for those belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle.
Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, with unblinking eyes, said this to the Blessed One:

"Listen to me, Blessed One, regarding this maṇḍala of the gateway to liberation, which is honored by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the sake of the great mass of beings."
For the sake of welfare, happiness, and liberation,
homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas established throughout the three times. Homage to the Saṅghas of Pratyekabuddhas and noble Śrāvakas of the past, future, and present.
Homage to those who have attained the right path! Homage to those who have practiced correctly!
Homage to Śāradvatīputra, the one of great intelligence!
Homage to the assembly of great bodhisattvas, headed by the noble Maitreya.
Homage to the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Buddhas, headed by Supratiṣṭhitaśailendrarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇasupratibhāsavinivartiteśvararāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha. Homage to the Tathāgata Supratiṣṭhitamaṇikūṭarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaraśmyudgataśrīkūṭarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipaśyin. Homage to the Tathāgata Śikhin.
Homage to the Tathāgata Viśvabhū. Homage to the Tathāgata Krakucchanda. Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakamuni.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kāśyapa! Homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha! It is as follows:
Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā!
Oṃ śame śame mahāśame! Protect, protect me and all sentient beings; O you who pacify all evil, svāhā!
Homage to the Tathāgata Suparikīrtitanāmadheya! Homage to the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī!
Homage to the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnaprabhāseśvararāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Apratihatabhaiṣajyarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vikrāntagāmin.
Homage to the Buddha.
Homage to the Dharma.
Homage to the Saṅgha!
Homage to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present! It is as follows:

O increaser of mindfulness, increaser of intelligence, increaser of conduct, increaser of steadfastness, increaser of wisdom, increaser of eloquence, increaser of meditation, increaser of concentration, increaser of tranquility!
Increasing insight;
increasing all factors conducive to awakening; for the fulfillment of all Buddha-qualities, svāhā!
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One. Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Great Compassionate One.

Having paid homage to these, I shall now recite this Heart-mantra named Amoghapāśarāja, which was uttered from the mouth of the Noble Avalokiteśvara and spoken in the presence of the Tathāgata amidst a great assembly.

May my mantra-words be effective; may all my undertakings be accomplished; and may there be protection for me and for all sentient beings from all fears. It is as follows: Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu mara mara miri miri muru muru Mahākāruṇika!
Sara sara, śiri śiri, suru suru, curu curu, ciri ciri, viri viri, miri miri, O you who hold the great lotus in your hand!
Kala kala, kili kili, kulu kulu, O Great Pure Being!
Buddhya buddhya, bodha bodha, bodhi bodhi, awaken, awaken, O Supreme Pure Being! Kaṇa kaṇa, kiṇi kiṇi, kuṇu kuṇu!
Kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru, O Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
Cala cala saṃcala saṃcala vicala vicala pracala pracala eṭaṭa eṭaṭa bhara bhara bhiri bhiri bhuru bhuru tara tara tiri tiri turu turu, come, come, O Mahākāruṇika!
O you who wear the guise of Mahāpaśupati!
Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara para para vara vara mara mara lara lara hara hara hāhā hīhī hūhū oṃ-kāra-brahmaveśadhara!
Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara nara nara vara!
O Bestower of Boons! O You whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of rays! Hara hara! Blaze, blaze! Heat, heat! Shine, shine!
Wander, wander!
O Blessed One, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods and ṛṣis, including Soma, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, Brahmā, Indra, Vāyu, Agni, and Dhanada!

*Suru suru curu curu muru muru dhuru dhuru,* you who assume many various forms as Sanatkumāra, Rudra, Vāsava, Viṣṇu, Dhanada, Vāyu, Agni, the Leader of Sages, Vināyaka, and others; *dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara,* O Giver of Boons, Avalokiteśvara, adorned with all virtues, Lord of the World who gazes upon all beings from every side, Great Lord, Lord of the Three Worlds! Avalokiteśvara, [I take refuge in you]. Please grant me protection. Please grant me safety. Please grant me peace. Please grant me happiness. Please grant me the attainment of all my wishes. Please grant me the fulfillment of all my aspirations. Please grant me the removal of all suffering. Please grant me the destruction of all obstacles. Please grant me the purification of all sins. Please grant me the increase of all merit. Please grant me the realization of the Bodhi-mind. Please grant me the attainment of the stage of non-retrogression. Please grant me the vision of all Buddhas. Please grant me the hearing of the Dharma of all Buddhas. Please grant me the service of all Buddhas. Please grant me the protection of all Bodhisattvas. Please grant me the support of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas. Please grant me the assistance of all devas and nāgas. Please grant me the aid of all yakṣas and gandharvas. Please grant me the help of all asuras and garuḍas. Please grant me the favor of all kinnaras and mahoragas. Please grant me the blessing of all humans and non-humans. Please grant me the empowerment of all Tathāgatas. Please grant me the transmission of the seal of all Dharmas. Please grant me the entry into the realm of all Samādhis. Please grant me the mastery of all mantras and vidyās. Please grant me the accomplishment of all mudrās. Please grant me the fulfillment of all vows. Please grant me the attainment of all supernatural powers. Please grant me the liberation from all saṃsāra. Please grant me the arrival at the shore of Nirvāṇa. Please grant me the realization of the nature of all phenomena. Please grant me the awakening to the essence of the mind. Please grant me the perfection of all roots of goodness. Please grant me the vajra of the indestructible mind. Please grant me the thunderbolt of the Great Power. Please grant me the fire of the Wisdom of Burning. Please grant me the water of the Great Purity. Please grant me the earth of the Great Stability. Please grant me the wind of the Great Movement. Please grant me the space of the Great Emptiness. Please grant me the treasury of the inexhaustible Dharma. Please grant me the storehouse of the unconditioned. Please grant me the gate of the Dharma-realm. Please grant me the path of the Bodhisattva. Please grant me the vehicle of the Mahāyāna. Please grant me the city of Nirvāṇa. Please grant me the garden of the Bodhi-tree. Please grant me the pond of the Eightfold Noble Path. Please grant me the lotus of the Three Jewels. Please grant me the fragrance of the ten powers. Please grant me the radiance of the four fearlessnesses. Please grant me the sound of the eighteen unique qualities. Please grant me the majesty of the thirty-two marks. Please grant me the brilliance of the Buddha’s mind. Please grant me the sovereignty of the Buddha’s deeds. Please grant me the leadership of the Buddha’s assembly. Muhu muhu, muru muru, muya muya, muñca muñca! Protect, protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes, from all seizing spirits, from all diseases, from all poisons, and from all fevers!
Likewise, bind, bind [all harm]! O deliverer from binding, beating, threatening, kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons!
Kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara ciri ciri curu curu, O illuminator of the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the four noble truths!
Tapa tapa tama tama dama dama śama śama masa masa dhama dhama, O Greatly Compassionate One, O dispeller of the great darkness of ignorance, O fulfiller of the six perfections!
Mala mala mili mili mulu mulu ṭaṭa ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu, O you who have made a girdle of eneya-deer skin, come, come, O Greatly Compassionate One!
O shatterer of the hosts of spirits belonging to Īśvara, Maheśvara, and Mahābhūta;

*kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru para para hara hara vara vara sara sara mara mara kara kara kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi kiṭi kuṭu kuṭu maṭa maṭa*, O dweller in the realm of the Great Purification, O Greatly Compassionate One!

O you who wear a white sacrificial thread and a jewel crown and garland; O you whose head is adorned with matted locks upon the crown of the Omniscient One; O you whose palm is graced by the most wonderful lotus; O you who are unshakable through meditative concentration, absorption, and liberation; O protector of the continuities of many beings; O Greatly Compassionate One; O purifier of all karmic obscurations; O fulfiller of the wisdom of omniscience;
O liberator from all diseases; O fulfiller of the hopes of all beings; O bringer of consolation to all beings—homage be to you, svāhā!
Svāhā to Amogha! Svāhā to Amoghapāśa! Svāhā to Ajita!
Svāhā to Aparājitā!
Svāhā to Amitābha! Svāhā to the Son of Amitābha!
Svāhā to the crushing of Māra’s army!
Svāhā to fearlessness, the bestower of fearlessness!
Svāhā to victory!
Svāhā to Vijaya!
Svāhā to Jayavijaya! Svāhā to Varada!
Svāhā to the bestower of boons!
Svāhā to the pacifier of untimely death!
And perform this rite for me; homage be to you, svāhā!
oṃ raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ jaya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ jra jiṃ juṃ phaṭ svāhā /
Oṃ hūṃ jaya svāhā / Oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśāpratihata hrīḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ vasumati svāhā /
Oṃ ārolīk svāhā / Oṃ bahule bahule svāhā / Oṃ ārolik hrīḥ hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā /
O Blessed One, bring about the complete destruction, without remainder, of my unwholesome karma that is to be experienced as either determinate or indeterminate; svāhā!
To the one with the lotus in hand, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, svāhā!
The ritual applications of this mantra, which is perfected through recitation, are as follows:
by reciting it at the three times of day, one purifies the five deeds of immediate retribution and brings about the purification of all karmic obscurations.

A boundary is established by means of agalloch incense; for all fevers, a thread should be tied with ashes, water, mustard seeds, khadira-wood pegs, and so forth. For all diseases, ghee, oil, or water should be given after having been consecrated with mantras.
There is also the cutting of magical spells (*kākhorda*) with a weapon and the [binding of] a protective thread.
For abdominal pain, salt water mixed with clay or simply water destroys the poison.
For eye disease, a white thread should be tied around the ear.
For toothache, a *karavīra* wood tooth-stick should be used.

Having recited the *sīmābandha* mantra twenty-one times over a five-colored thread, one should tie it to four stakes made of *khadira* wood and drive them into the ground in the four directions; thus there will be a boundary-binding.
This may be done with a protective thread, water, or ashes.
For all planetary seizures (*graha*), a five-colored thread is used.

In all fevers, one should use a white thread. For snake-bites, insect-stings, scabies, and throat-inflammations, [one should use] honey and long pepper (*pippalī*). For eye diseases, one should use fragrant water, *palāśa* water, or licorice (*madhuyaṣṭī*) water. For all quarrels, strife, and disputes, as well as for false accusations, one should recite the mantra over water and wash one's face with it.

In cases of calamities affecting foreign territories, kingdoms, or nations, one should place a full jar there; then, being pure and dressed in clean garments, having performed a great worship, the text should be recited, and a great peace (*mahāśānti*) will ensue.
One should sprinkle with that water, and protection will be established for all sentient beings;
all calamities and misfortunes will be pacified.
Having recited [the mantra] twenty-one times over a sandalwood tilaka mark, it should be applied to the heart; all acts of immediate retribution (ānantarya) will be exhausted.
Through constant recitation, there is protection of the home;
through a lotus-homa, there is protection of all sentient beings;
through a sandalwood-homa, there is protection against all grahas, bhūtas, and nakṣatras.
Jayā, Vijayā, Aparājitā, Nākulī, Gandhanākūlī, Dhāraṇī, Abhayapāṇi, Indriyapāṇi, Gandhapriyaṅgu, Tagara, Cakrā, Mahācakrā, Vikrāntā, Somarājī, and Sunandā—
having consecrated a jewel by reciting [the mantra] over it one hundred and eight times as available, it should be worn on the head or the arm.
When placed around the necks of children or women, it brings about supreme good fortune.
(Āṭānāṭika Sūtra 169) It pacifies misfortune and bestows sons.
By binding this gem, all protection is secured;
poison and fire do not prevail, and no harm caused by poison arises.
Even if pain has arisen, it will not cause further affliction; they will quickly pacify it.
It will pacify malevolent planets; by means of water and the *karavīra* creeper, it performs the subduing of wind, clouds, and thunderbolts, and accomplishes all rites.
This heart-mantra of the noble Avalokiteśvara is supremely efficacious; even when unaccomplished through formal ritual, it performs these very deeds.

Then, desiring to accomplish [the rite], the practitioner should have an image of the Buddha painted on a cloth using all the colors; likewise, having had the noble Avalokiteśvara painted by a painter observing the *poṣadha* vows— [Avalokiteśvara] wearing a crown of matted hair, clad in a lower garment of deerskin, assuming the attire of Paśupati, and adorned with all ornaments.
It should be painted.
Then, the practitioner, having fashioned a mandala before it out of fallen cow dung and scattering white flowers upon it, should place eight jars filled with scented water;
there should be eight offerings and sixty-four ritual implements.
Excluding offerings of meat and blood, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times while burning aloeswood incense.

Having fasted for either one day and night or three nights, or having consumed only the three white foods, and having bathed at the three times of day, one should perform the recitation while clad in clean garments.
Then, one sees oneself and the image depicted before it; upon seeing this, one rejoices until the Noble Avalokiteśvara himself arrives.
It fulfills all hopes.
Or, having recited the mantra over realgar ointment and applied it to the eyes,
one then becomes invisible and travels through the sky.

He attains the samādhi named "Array of Non-deluded Knowledge," whereby the practitioner accomplishes exactly whatever he desires. Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and those monks were uplifted in spirit.
And those bodhisattvas, those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas,
rejoiced in what was spoken by the Blessed One.
Thus ends the Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled the Heart of the Amoghapāśa.
